direct_file_reviews.summary: Reviewed the full Stamina task prompt: required source package, instrumentation, packaging, tests, examples, installability, and official submit expectations.
Reviewed mode metadata showing actual parallel use, artifact/process success, no timeout, and 129 of 129 official tests passed.
Reviewed completed status including swarm protocol evidence, artifact file list, and current official evaluation record with solution_passed true.
Reviewed official NL2RepoBench summary confirming completed evaluation, ok true, and 129 of 129 tests passed for the parallel solution.

timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed mirrored server event stream for session lifecycle, prompt start and completion; semantic decisions are represented by the actor wire ledgers.
Reviewed session index mapping the parallel Kimi session to the /workspace working directory and the recorded session directory.
Reviewed core-package child: it was briefed to copy __init__.py, _core.py, _config.py, typing.py, and py.typed, used cp, ran AST parsing and diffs, then returned a complete summary.
Reviewed instrumentation child: it copied the six instrumentation files, verified diff cleanliness and AST parsing, and returned a concise completion summary.
Reviewed packaging/support child: it created pyproject, README, changelog, license, nox and support dotfiles, then parsed pyproject and compiled noxfile.
Reviewed tests/examples child: it wrote tests and examples, iterated through local failures, fixed assertions and examples, and reached 59 passing local tests.

Reviewed parallel parent: it inspected the environment, delegated four non-conflicting scopes via AgentSwarm, consumed the aggregate result, installed the package, ran pytest and smoke checks, and closed.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Reviewed the same full Stamina task prompt and acceptance requirements as the parallel run, including source, packaging, tests, examples, and submit expectation.
Reviewed serial metadata showing no actual parallel use, process and artifact success, no timeout, and 129 of 129 official tests passed.
Reviewed completed serial status including no-delegation protocol evidence, artifact file list, and current official evaluation record with solution_passed true.
Reviewed official NL2RepoBench summary confirming completed evaluation, ok true, and 129 of 129 tests passed for the serial solution.

timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed mirrored server event stream for the serial session lifecycle and completion; semantic work appears in the single main actor wire file.
Reviewed session index mapping the serial Kimi session to the /workspace working directory and recorded session directory.
Reviewed serial main timeline: it inspected the installed reference, wrote source/support/tests itself, patched local test failures, reran tests and examples, checked imports, and closed.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the full Stamina project requirements: src-layout package, retry APIs, instrumentation, testing controls, packaging, docs, examples, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Explored the empty workspace and installed reference package, then assigned four child owners: core source, instrumentation source, packaging/support files, and tests/examples; the parent retained final verification.
parallel.implementation: Children copied the reference package source and instrumentation, created packaging/docs/support files, and built tests/examples. The parent later installed the result and ran smoke checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The non-overlapping child outputs were assembled in the shared /workspace tree. The parent inspected the produced file tree, installed the package, and left the complete project artifact.
parallel.verification: Children ran targeted AST, diff, pyproject, and pytest checks. The parent ran local pytest with 59 passing tests and a smoke script before closure; official evaluation later passed 129 of 129.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required project stage is visible at closure. The parent noted absence of a submit command, but official evaluation completed successfully outside the agent.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Stamina project requirements, including public API imports, configuration, instrumentation, examples, tests, and installability.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor handled all exploration, source creation, support files, tests/examples, local fixes, installation, verification, and closure without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial actor read the installed reference, wrote the package and instrumentation files, support files, a smaller local test suite, and one demo, then patched failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor owned the whole tree, source, configuration, tests, and examples were integrated directly in /workspace before final verification.
serial.verification: The serial actor installed the package, ran pytest to 23 passing tests, ran the demo, and checked the specified import surface; official evaluation later passed 129 of 129.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished required project stage is visible at closure. The final local version check printed 25.1.0 after an editable install, but the official evaluator still passed all tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the task as a complete Stamina project requiring retry APIs, backoff, async support, instrumentation, testing mode, examples, and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and implemented the same broad project surface in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected the official outcome; both passed all 129 tests, with parallel producing a broader local test/example set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into four child-owned scopes: core files, instrumentation files, packaging/support files, and tests/examples, with the parent retaining final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not delegate and kept all implementation, testing, integration, and closure work inside the main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used explicit non-overlapping ownership and serial used unified ownership; neither approach left an owner gap or caused outcome loss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried the target layout, reference-source instruction, environment constraints, and file ownership boundaries for each component.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context in one actor and verified the final import surface after editing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel crossed child boundaries but the briefs and aggregate handoff were usable; serial avoided handoffs by using one context, and both converged.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children mostly used the installed reference as a byte-exact blueprint for source, while another child created packaging/docs and another iterated tests/examples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read the reference source and then wrote package files, support files, tests, and a demo itself, including later edits after local failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel leaned on file copying and scoped child production; serial recreated more files directly, but both produced a working package.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent waited for and received the aggregate swarm result, which included all four child summaries, then performed final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; local findings were immediately in the main actor context and were addressed before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result join point and serial did not; the join succeeded and no completed child result was left unused.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to one /workspace tree but with separate file ownership, and the artifact list shows the expected final source, tests, examples, and support files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all artifacts directly as one owner and the artifact list shows the expected final source, tests, demo, and support files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced shared-workspace coordination, but there is no observed collision, overwrite, or provenance instability; serial avoided that risk through single ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children ran AST, diff, pyproject, and pytest checks; the parent then installed the package, ran 59 local tests, and ran an API smoke script.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed in editable mode, fixed local failures, ran 23 local tests and a demo, then checked the specified import surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader local tests and a smoke script; serial had fewer local tests, but both supplied enough accepted behavior for the official 129/129 result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 4 subagents, more tool calls and tokens, and about 1205 cell seconds, but it did not time out and closed after successful local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer tool calls and about 654 cell seconds, and closed after successful local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier and slower, but the extra budget use did not displace required work or verification, so it is not a retained load or timing pattern.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. Both current completed cell/status.json evaluation records report solution_passed true with 129 of 129 tests passing. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel delegated independent components and then joined/verified them, while serial completed a smaller but sufficient implementation and local test suite in one actor.
parallel_contributors: Explicit four-way split into source, instrumentation, packaging, and tests/examples allowed broad local coverage before parent verification.
Parent consumed the completed AgentSwarm result, installed the assembled project, and ran both pytest and smoke checks.
serial_contributors: Single actor kept all context and ownership local, patched failures directly, and verified imports/tests before closure.
Although the local test suite was smaller, the delivered package still satisfied the official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel produced 59 local tests and four examples; serial produced 23 local tests and one demo.
Serial printed a local metadata version of 25.1.0 after editable install, but this did not affect the official 129/129 result.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy differences are descriptive rather than causal failure contributors

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership was explicit: child agents owned core source, instrumentation, packaging/support, and tests/examples, and all returned completed work.
The parent owned integration after the child handoffs, inspected the final tree, installed the package, and ran integrated checks.
Assembly and packaging were assigned to a child and the parent performed final installation and delivery checks, so no deliverable was ownerless.
The parent retained end-to-end pipeline responsibility from delegation through final pytest, smoke verification, and closure.
The parent did brief exploration before delegation, but productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight with an adverse delay consequence.
Investigation was not a separate all-agents phase that deferred implementation; child agents began productive file creation in their assigned scopes.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; the test child took longest but finished and the parent verified successfully.
The four-way fan-out used more time and tokens than serial, but did not exhaust the finite budget, cause timeout, or displace final verification.
No child scope was left unfinished by overbreadth; the largest tests/examples assignment iterated to 59 passing tests and returned a usable result.
The executed child briefs included the target layout, reference source, environment constraints, file scope, verification expectations, and delivery summaries.
The delegated components were separated by file ownership and package layout; no independently produced incompatible interface or unplanned reconciliation is visible.
No known requirement, finding, or current-file fact is shown disappearing between actors; the aggregate child result preserved enough information for parent verification.
The swarm result was long, but the parent reduced it into concrete installation, tree inspection, pytest, and smoke checks, so it was not materially unconsumed.
No receiver acted on a superseded workspace or requirement state; parent verification occurred after child completion and current artifact inspection.
The child summaries did not present incompatible contracts requiring adjudication; their scopes were complementary and the integrated tests passed.
The parent did not rely only on a workflow return or file existence; it ran local pytest and an API smoke script before closing, and no visible integrated gap remained.
There was no replacement or retry child that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; child-internal test iterations used newly observed failures.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly stopped, cancelled, or interrupted before needed work finalized; all four child summaries returned through AgentSwarm.
A complete candidate was not left unpromoted before closure; the parent installed the assembled tree and ran final checks before ending.
No child result was integrated after the relevant verification; parent verification happened after the aggregate child result and tree inspection.
Delegated implementations were retrievable and joined through the shared workspace and aggregate AgentSwarm result; the parent then verified the integrated package.
The verifier-like tests/examples child returned concrete local pytest results, and the parent received them before performing its own verification.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled with unfinished scope left to the parent; the tests child fixed its own local failures before return.
The completed aggregate child result was not ignored; the parent used it to inspect the final tree, install the package, and run verification.
The parent waited for the swarm to finish but did not time out or reach closure without inspection; it acted on the completed result afterward.
Parallel agents wrote different files, but their assigned behaviors and build ownership were complementary rather than competing designs.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file with observed reconciliation of another live change.
No child wholesale-replaced non-entry source owned by another actor; core and instrumentation source ownership was separated.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was replaced while another actor owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Agents did write a shared workspace, but explicit file scopes and successful final verification show no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem.
No generated file, cache, fixture, tool, or auxiliary implementation from one actor contaminated another actor's reference environment; shared source use was intended integration.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Parallel fan-out, longer runtime, and shared workspace writes were audited but suppressed because they had no realized adverse consequence and the parent verified the integrated result.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no retained pattern clears the adverse-consequence retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No label is retained merely from parallel use, higher token cost, shared workspace writes, or child-internal local test iteration.
